title: Hearts of three vertebrates
body: In a biology class, students compared the hearts of three animals. A fish has a heart with only two chambers: blood is pumped to the gills, is oxygenated there, and passes directly to the rest of the body, so it goes through the heart only once in each cycle. A frog has a three-chambered heart, and some mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood takes place; the frog's body temperature changes with the temperature of its surroundings. A pigeon, like a human being, has a four-chambered heart in which the right and left sides are completely separated, so oxygenated and deoxygenated blood never mix. Blood passes through the pigeon's heart twice in each cycle through the body. The pigeon keeps its body temperature nearly constant whether the day is hot or cold, and it is very active, flying long distances.
